dataset_name: Fantasy Draft Brain - COMPLETE TEST BUILD
status: PROVISIONAL COMPLETE TEST DATA - NOT FINAL DRAFT BOARD
important_note: This file is intentionally complete enough to test the app. Baseline ranks come from Jamie Calandro/RotoBaller Aug. 26 Top 250. Transcript-researched players contain our custom intelligence. market_adp is a temporary proxy unless market_adp_quality says otherwise; replace with final Yahoo/market ADP at Sept. 1 freeze. Deep transcript targets outside the baseline top 200 have been appended so the final-round recommendation logic can be tested.

sources.name: Project transcript digest
sources.use: Primary custom player thesis and contradiction tracker

recommendation_rules: Use one master player pool; each player is marked drafted only once.
14-team RB scarcity is a major adjustment. Protect against RB tier cliffs.
Full PPR boosts reliable WR volume and pass-catching RBs, but one flex does not erase RB scarcity.
Do not force QB early; increase urgency when only 1-2 QBs remain in the last preferred tier.
Elite-or-wait at TE unless a mid-tier TE has legitimate target-leader upside.
Tier cliffs matter more than tiny ranking differences.
Late bench spots favor contingent RBs and breakout WRs over backup QB/TE and low-ceiling veterans.
Current price matters. A good player can become a bad pick if taken too early.
K and DST are streaming positions. Suppress them from recommendations until the final rounds.
For K/DST, prioritize Weeks 1-2 matchup quality rather than season-long name value.

draft_slot_notes.early: Long waits after picks. Secure tier-ending players before the wrap; do not assume a target survives 20+ selections.
draft_slot_notes.middle: Most flexible slot. Let value fall, but react to RB and QB tier endings.
draft_slot_notes.late: Use paired picks intentionally: one scarcity/tier-cliff pick plus one best-value/upside pick.

injury_logic.rule: Current availability and long-term durability are separate. Multi-week stashes are more expensive in a six-bench, one-IR league.
